title: Arasecoseagge
summary: Arasecoseagge is recorded as a Babylon placename for the easternmost East Neck, also known in English as Captain Fleet's Neck. The name designated the meadow portion of the neck, while Anuskkummikak referred to the upland.
address_label: Argyle Park / Captain Fleet's Neck area, Babylon, NY (approximate)
map_geometry_source: Approximate modern point near Argyle Park/Babylon for the meadow portion of Captain Fleet's Neck; not an exact historic coordinate.
why_this_matters: Arasecoseagge preserves a Native name for the meadow portion of Captain Fleet's Neck, interpreted as the furthermost meadow. The name distinguishes wet meadowland from nearby upland and shows how local geography could be described with ecological precision. A colonial deed reference becomes evidence of Native land knowledge, where meadows, necks, and shorelines were part of an understood South Shore landscape.
translation_content:
Alternate forms include Arascascagge and Awrasse-cas-cagge. The name is interpreted as the furthermost meadow, connecting arase with words meaning beyond or furthermost and coseagge with a meadow term.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names are expressions of societies and cultures, and so also have an effect on cultural and geographical image.”

— Nurettin Özgen and Volkan İdris Sarı, The Place of Names within the Context of Political Ideologies (2021), abstract
whereintheworld_content: Arasecoseagge preserves a specific land-use distinction within a larger neck of land. Keeping it separate from the upland name Anuskkummikak helps show that Native place names could describe different parts of the same landscape with precision.
